fixed.explanation: filterCookies prefixed a dot to every cookie domain, so host-only cookies matched subdomains. It also used a plain string prefix for paths. It now matches host-only cookies by exact hostname, matches dotted domains by exact name or suffix, and matches paths per RFC 6265 5.1.4 (exact, or a prefix ending at a slash boundary). pathMatches in cookieStore.ts no longer appends a slash to the request path, so cookie path /foo/ no longer matches request /foo. It still matches /apiv2 against /api only on a slash boundary.

query.intent: The cookie URL filter (filterCookies) used for listing cookies prepends a dot to every cookie domain and compares paths with plain string prefix. It should implement RFC 6265 domain-match (host-only cookies match only the exact host) and path-match (exact or slash boundary). Also the path check used when sending cookies (domainMatches/pathMatches in network cookie store) appends a slash to the request path, making /foo match /foo/.
query.symptom: Listing cookies for URLs returns host-only cookies for subdomains and for path prefixes like /apiv2, and a cookie with path /foo/ is sent to /foo.

history.analysis: filterCookies in network.ts prepends a dot to every cookie domain and uses a plain startsWith for paths, which matches the reported bug. pathMatches in cookieStore.ts appends a slash to the request path, so /foo matches /foo/. Both need to change. domainMatches in cookieStore.ts already handles host-only cookies correctly, so filterCookies can reuse it.
